title: To each his very own VR
author: remorej
selftext:
Few months ago I went through the Bobiverse series in rapid succession. Each Bob creates a personalized virtual environment. I remember how Hiro wrote the sword-fighting software in Snow Crash.

I've been experimenting with [Hyperfy](https://github.com/hyperfy-xyz/hyperfy), an open-source engine for multiplayer 3D worlds. Hyperfy is quite literally a website, built with JavaScript, React and Three.js, running directly in the browser. You host your own world on your own server, just like any website, and visitors only need a URL. You own the source code and can customize the engine itself.

I love astronomy, and [my own fork](https://github.com/jerometremblay/hyperfy) has a ridiculously detailed night sky. Yesterday I integrated [the engine of tailuge/billards](https://github.com/tailuge/billiards), and now i have an amazingly realistic pool table. 15 minutes of Sol 6.1 Medium. Everything you see in my world is generated by ChatGPT or Codex via a [3d-prompt box](https://github.com/jerometremblay/hyperfy#build-with-a-prompt-box) that export a zip file with all models, and merge them back into the world afterward.

I know that many of us (and I include myself in that) don't really want to run vibe coded applications from stangers. That's perfectly fine. Vibe code it yourself then. Fork the canonical Hyperfy repo, and start from there. It's a solid baseline. And if you visit me through a portal, you have my own runtime neatly sandboxed in your browser.

Each world is independent, portals can connect them as links connect web pages and we transition seamlessly from homepage to homeworld.
